title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from budget boosts to new partnerships. Startups are eyeing defense contracts while established players grapple with setbacks and advancements.

themes.title: Defense Contracts on the Rise
themes.body: The Space Force's new playbook aims to streamline access for startups seeking defense business, indicating a shift towards greater commercial integration. Meanwhile, the FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to space resilience, highlighting the growing importance of defense in space.

themes.title: Rocketry Setbacks and Advances
themes.body: China is gearing up to launch its latest batch of reusable rockets, showcasing its continued ambition in space. In contrast, the New Glenn rocket's explosion at Cape Canaveral serves as a stark reminder of the inherent risks in this high-stakes industry.

themes.title: Data as a Strategic Asset
themes.body: The utilization of spatial data in the US-Iran conflict underscores its emerging role as a weapon of war. This trend is further reflected in companies like Slingshot, which are strategically positioning themselves to provide military-grade space domain awareness.

themes.title: Investment Trends in Space
themes.body: True Anomaly's recent $190 million Series C funding round signals robust investor interest in space tech. Additionally, the defense-tech IPO window appears to be inching open, suggesting a potential wave of public offerings in the near future.
